latestPosts.caption: Many people might not know that the @nycmarathon is shepherded by a nonprofit called New York Road Runners, who are responsible for producing what might be the single most unifying event of the year. Not only is the marathon a great service to runners, it a great service to the New York community. Additionally the @nyrr holds numerous year-long programs for youth and adults which grow the popularity of the sport globally. This year marks the 50th anniversary of the five-borough race, and I was so happy to partner with NYRR to share the stories of two special NYC marathon runners. Congratulations to Laura and everyone else who ran and finished their own marathon stories today, and a big thank you to New York Road Runners for their important work inspiring people globally to experience the power of running.

latestPosts.caption: Hart Island is New York City’s public cemetery and the final resting place for more than one million people buried in mass graves. Elsie Soto is the Director of Friends of Hart Island, a family-led initiative dedicated to honoring those buried on Hart Island and supporting their loved ones. Her organization works to challenge the stigma surrounding Hart Island, raise public awareness, and advocate for expanded visitation, improved transportation, and historic preservation. I’m very grateful for the time she spent with me.

latestPosts.caption: “There was a bad break up, sort of. It was eight months ago. I’m past it now. But I had to experience that for the first time. I don’t think I handled it as well as I could. At the time I couldn’t grasp that maybe it wasn’t anybody’s fault. Maybe I just wanted to be with the person for longer than they wanted to be with me. But accepting things that you don’t want to happen is really, really hard. It’s like: ‘Why do they get to walk around, and keep living their life, while I’m miserable all the time?’ It didn’t seem fair. So I might have reacted in a way that was disproportionate, to make the person feel more guilty than they needed to. Sometimes that’s your only recourse when someone hurts you: feeling aggrieved, and making it known. Not that it keeps you from suffering. But there is a sense of power in it. It allows you to redistribute the pain that you’re feeling. You can make their life a hassle for a bit, hurt their feelings, tell everyone they’re a big asshole. When the truth is: maybe they were just living their life, trying their best, and you got hurt. There’s not always a villain. Sometimes you just get fucked up by somebody exercising their own autonomy.”

latestPosts.caption: Twenty-five years ago Tyree Bacon entered the South Tower of the World Trade Center with three of his colleagues, but he was the only one who would return. This is the story of Tyree, his colleagues, and the unknown woman who saved his life. This story was written at the request of @zohrankmamdani as part of a series his office was compiling on the stories of first responders. I’m very grateful for their initiative and assistance, especially the wonderful @karamccurdy.
